    AI Overview
    NASA is set to launch
    Artemis II, the first crewed Moon mission since 1972, no earlier than April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. EDT from Kennedy Space Center. Four astronauts will conduct a 10-day, around-the-moon test flight, paving the way for future lunar landings. Live coverage is available via NASA+, YouTube, and Amazon Prime. 
    Mission Details & Key Information 
    • Mission Goal: A 10-day crewed test flight around the Moon, testing the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule.
    • Crew: Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen.
    • Launch Window: The primary launch window opens on April 1, 2026, with an 80% chance of favorable weather, primarily monitoring for clouds and wind.
    • Trajectory: The crew will fly beyond the Moon, perform a U-turn, and return, a practice mission for future, long-term lunar habitation.
    • Visibility: The launch is expected to be visible from parts of Florida and southern Georgia. 
    Follow-up Artemis Missions 
    • Artemis III: Planned as the first human landing in this program, aiming to land astronauts on the lunar surface, with potential adjustments in strategy and timing to ensure safety.
    • SpaceX Partnership: SpaceX is developing the Starship Human Landing System and targeting uncrewed lunar landing tests in 2027. 
    The mission marks a major return to the Moon, focusing on lunar exploration and preparing for eventual human journeys to Mars.

    Date. When was the first moon landing?
    About this result
    Feedback
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    The first manned moon landing occurred on July 20, 1969, during NASA's Apollo 11 mission. American astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin landed the Lunar Module Eagle at 4:17 p.m. EDT, with Armstrong becoming the first person to walk on the moon later that evening at 10:56 p.m. EDT. 
    Key Facts About the First Moon Landing:
    • Mission: Apollo 11. 
    • Date: July 20, 1969 (Landing), July 21, 1969 (First Step). 
    • Astronauts: Neil Armstrong, Buzz Aldrin, and Michael Collins (Command Module Pilot who stayed in orbit). 
    • Location: The Moon's Sea of Tranquility. 
    • Famous Quote: "That's one small step for [a] man, one giant leap for mankind" — Neil Armstrong. 
    • Return: The crew splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean on July 24, 1969. 
    The mission was a major milestone in the 1960s Space Race and fulfilled President Kennedy's national goal of landing a human on the moon before the decade's end.

      Apollo 11
      Apollo 11. Apollo 11 was the first mission to land humans on the Moon. It fulfilled a 1961 goal set by President John F. Kennedy to send American astronauts to the surface and return them safely to Earth before the end of the decade.

      Purpose. What was the purpose of the moon landing?
      Feedback
      The primary objective of Apollo 11 was to complete a national goal set by President John F. Kennedy on May 25, 1961: perform a crewed lunar landing and return to Earth. Astronaut Buzz Aldrin stands on the Moon facing a U.S. flag during the Apollo 11 mission in July 1969.

      Legacy. What is the legacy of the moon landing?
      Feedback
      Revolution in Lunar Science

      For the first time in history, scientists could analyze samples from another world. This allowed them to determine the age, composition, and other properties of the Moon and to learn more about the solar system itself.
